Quarterly Update
Since June, WFP resumed its regular in-camp e-voucher programme in collaboration with the TurkishRed Crescent (TRC), providing around 53,000 beneficiaries in eight camps in the southeast with amonthly assistance of Turkish Lira (TRY) 300 (US$ 11) per person. This caseload includes additionalearthquake-affected Syrians who took shelter in the camps after the earthquakes of 6 February2023. Also in June, WFP and TRC increased the monthly assistance amount from TRY 230 (US$ 8.5) toTRY 300 (US$ 11). This increase is aligned with the Social Safety Net (SSN) transfer value.
Monitoring
The food basket cost in the contracted shops in the eight operational camps increased fromTRY 677.36 (US$ 25) to TRY 802.89 (US$ 29.8) between July and September, representing a 19percent increase. Meanwhile, in collaboration with TRC, WFP teams resumed the work on thecomprehensive needs assessment of refugees living in seven camps as of July—excluding theElazig camp which hosts Ukranian refugees. The assessment was first initiated in Q4 2022 andwas later interrupted with the occurance of the earthquakes in early 2023. The purpose of theassessment is to identify needs and vulnerability levels to ensure that assistance is provided tothe right people at the right time. The quantitative data collection was completed in September.The research team is planning to conduct qualitative data collection, using appropriate toolssuch as focus group discussions and key informant interviews, to triangulate the quantitativefindings. The results of the analysis will be discussed collaboratively among stakeholders in Q4to further inform programme design and targeting options.
E-Voucher Programme: Lifeline since 2012
